messages.author: c4e67f9d1aa89ddc
messages.subject: Step counting in GGIR ?
parts:
Hi Vincent and hi all, 

Although the community is moving away from step count has a index for physical activity, it remains frequently mentioned or requested; it may also be relevant in conditions specifically affecting gait abilities.

Does integrating this feature within GGIR  has been considered ?

Does anyone think about options to perform this ?

Best regards,

Damien

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Step counting in GGIR ?
parts:
Hi Damien,
Good suggestion and I agree that it is worth having this functionality in GGIR. 

R package GENEAclassify implemented two step count algorithms and this works for GENEActiv accelerometers.
The GPL license that package uses is not compatible with the LGPL license used by GGIR. GGIR would either have to adopt the GPL license as per the license conditions or get explicit permission from the GENEAclassify developers to copy their code.
Changing license is not an option for me, getting permission from GENEAclassify developers is worth trying but it would not be surprise me if they say no.

One idea could be to investigate the origin of their algorithm and if it is based on an open published algorithm then use that as a starting point for implementing it in GGIR.
Another approach could be to start from scratch, develop something new, and share that with the world alongside the insights gained along the way.

Possible ways forward:
- Someone volunteers to develop this.
- Someone pays me to (co-)develop this.
Depending on the amount of work that needs to be done it may be possible to turn this into a student project.

Best regards,
Vincent

Hi Vincent,

 

Thanks for you answer.

 

So I guess the first step would be to ask GENEAclassify developers if we can copy their code to use it in another package (I understand you think it’s unlikely but on the other hand, GGIR promotes GENEActiv and this is good for Active Insight business)

 

How can we do that, I can contact them if you which but maybe you will be more legit.

 

In either case (yes or no for GENEAclassify) should we open an issue on github and see if people around are wishing to contributes  ?

 

I may also have credit to put a student on this here in Paris but this might need better mentoring than I can provide for (properly) implementing this feature in GGIR.

 

Regarding literature and after a quick search, it seem there is a lot of things out there we could use as a basis.

 

To be continued,

Best,

 

Damien
